svg.text: +41 more genes fit (the full table is in the result and the MCP text)
Per gene, a logistic regression of mutated (yes/no) on cohort (“Early-onset CRC” = 1 against “Average-onset CRC”) and MSI_TYPE, TMB_SCORE (MSI_TYPE as categories
against its commonest value, TMB_SCORE as a number; a sample attribute is the patient's first sample's); the odds ratio is the cohort term's, Wald 95% CI, and q is
Benjamini–Hochberg over the 56 genes fit. Patients, not samples: a patient is mutated in a gene when any of their samples carries a called mutation in it, and is in a
gene's model only when one of their mutation panels covers it (or whole-exome) — panel-aware, so a patient not profiled for a gene is left out of that gene, never counted
as wild type. Tested: the 56 genes mutated in at least 5.0% (and 10) of the patients profiled for them, both cohorts together (at most 200). “Early-onset CRC”: 1,699
patients with a mutation panel, 1,693 with every covariate; “Average-onset CRC”: 3,149 patients with a mutation panel, 3,146 with every covariate. Beside each adjusted
odds ratio is the raw one with its two-sided Fisher p, on the same patients; 2 genes significant raw (Fisher p < 0.05) are not after adjustment (adjusted p ≥ 0.05). For 9
genes, a covariate category in which no patient (or every patient) was mutated was merged into its reference level, since it would separate. Adjustment removes only
what the covariates measure: a hypermutated tumour raises every gene's odds at once, which TMB or MSI status as a covariate absorbs and nothing else does. Cohorts
are expected not to share patients; a patient in both would count on both sides.
